items.quote: The man of God had replied, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!” And that is exactly what happened to him
items.contrast: The officer, rather than the man of God, is the person to whom the prediction applies.
items.reason: The final “him” refers to the officer who was addressed by the man of God. Resolving that reference identifies the officer as the person trampled.

items.quote: For I was commanded by the word of the Lord
items.contrast: The Lord’s command is the reason for the refusal; the amount of the king’s offer is only part of a rejected hypothetical.
items.reason: The man of God explicitly introduces the Lord’s command as his reason. Saying “even if” the king offered half his possessions rules out the offer’s size as the cause.

items.quote: Jeroboam did not change his evil ways
items.contrast: Jeroboam fails to change his ways, whereas appointing priests is something he does again.
items.reason: The passage explicitly negates changing his evil ways and then contrasts that failure with his renewed appointment of priests.

items.quote: When Athaliah heard the noise made by the guards and the people, she went to the people
items.contrast: Hearing the noise prompts Athaliah to go; seeing the king occurs only after she arrives.
items.reason: The sequence connects her going with the noise she hears. Her sight of the king is a later event and therefore cannot explain her initial decision to go.

items.quote: When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar and said, “Seize him!”
items.contrast: Jeroboam gives the order, while the man of God is the person the order targets.
items.reason: The king is the speaker and points toward the man of God when ordering others to seize “him,” resolving the pronoun’s reference.
